title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were stranded on San Francisco streets when their batteries depleted during severe Fourth of July traffic congestion. Multiple vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, became immobilized and required towing. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the road.

The failure happened in traffic prediction and energy management during deployment. The system was used in conditions it was not designed for: sustained gridlock lasting nearly two hours, with unplanned road closures and major event disruptions that the vehicles could not navigate around or adapt to. A human dispatcher with authority to reroute vehicles away from congestion, or a requirement to return vehicles to a charging location before departure during announced high-traffic periods, could have prevented the stranding.

It is not established whether the autonomous system's decision to continue driving through fireworks was the result of a sensing failure, a planning failure, or insufficient safety constraints on the vehicle's operation during the event.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries drained during severe Fourth of July traffic congestion on Saturday. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volumes, and unplanned road closures. Several vehicles required towing, and one caught fire after driving over fireworks on the road. Additionally, frustrated motorists reported being stuck in standstill traffic for nearly two hours while the vehicles were cleared from roadways.

Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. One passenger described the autonomous vehicle continuing to drive despite fireworks being set off nearby, raising safety concerns. Mayor Daniel Lurie acknowledged the post-fireworks congestion and urged patience while streets cleared. City officials said they would meet with public and private partners to improve traffic management for future events. This incident parallels a December incident when Waymo vehicles stalled during a power outage that affected traffic lights.
